title: Startup Circuit for Relaxation Oscillators with Low Functional Current and Minimal Area
problem: Low-power relaxation oscillators suffer from long startup times, which is critical in ultra-low-power applications like timekeeping and sensor interfaces. Existing startup circuits either increase functional current or require significant area overhead.
motivation: In 32 kHz, sub-100nW oscillators used for real-time clocking in IoT and ultra-low-power processors, startup time directly impacts power consumption and time-to-ready. Improving startup without increasing functional current or area enables better battery life and smaller chip area.
method: A two-stage startup technique that initializes the ring oscillator in open-loop mode (with injected current to charge internal nodes) and then switches to closed-loop once frequency settles. Uses current mirrors and digital circuits for lightweight implementation.
key_novelty: Open-to-closed-loop transition startup methodology that achieves 3x faster startup (466µs → 150µs) without increasing functional current; minimal area overhead using current mirrors and digital logic.
contributions: 3x improvement in startup time (466µs to 150µs) across PVT variations
Functional current maintained at 52 nanoamperes (no increase vs. baseline)
Lightweight circuit implementation requiring minimal area and leakage
Validated across ±10% voltage and -40°C to +125°C temperature range
±5% post-trim frequency variation across voltage and temperature
limitations: Abstract only; no detailed area comparison metrics provided; no power consumption breakdown during startup phase; comparison with other state-of-the-art startup techniques not included; frequency settling dynamics not analyzed.
